findings.title: Backup code alone can log in if any TOTP value is also sent
findings.body: The new backup-code branch in credentials authorize never checks the primary factor. Password verification only runs when credentials.totpCode is empty, and non-CAL users are rejected only when totpCode is empty. A caller who knows the email and one backup code can sign in by posting any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000") with that backup code and a wrong or empty password. The password check and the identity-provider check are both skipped, and a matching backup code creates a session. A backup code then replaces the password or the IdP login, not only the authenticator, which contradicts the UI copy. The disable endpoint does not have this hole: it verifies the CAL password before accepting a backup code. This branch must verify the primary factor even when totpCode is present, and a non-CAL account must not be able to finish credentials login with only a backup code.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: After a backup code matches, the handler nulls that array slot and writes the re-encrypted list with a plain read-modify-write. The user row is not locked and the write is not conditional on the ciphertext that was just read. Two overlapping logins with the same code both see it as unused and both get a session, so the code is not single-use. Two overlapping logins with different codes can also lose an update: each write is based on a stale list, and the last write puts the other code back. Consume the code in a transaction that locks the user row, or compare-and-swap on the previous ciphertext, and only then issue the session.

findings.title: Dismissing the backup-code step skips onEnable and loses the codes
findings.body: A successful TOTP enable used to call onEnable() immediately. It now only moves to the backup-code step, and onEnable() runs only from the Close button. The dialog still takes onOpenChange, so Escape, the overlay, or the X control closes it without onEnable() or resetState(). Two-factor is already enabled on the server, but the parent is not notified, so the settings switch stays off and a later toggle tries to enable again and fails as already enabled. The codes live only in this component's state, are never shown again, and there is no regenerate action, so that dismiss also permanently drops the only copy. A refresh on this step has the same result. Block dismissal until the user finishes, or treat every close of this step as completion and call onEnable().

findings.title: Download control nests a button in an anchor inside the enable form
findings.body: The download control is a Button wrapped in an anchor with the blob URL, inside the form whose submit handler is handleEnable. Interactive content inside an anchor is invalid HTML, and browsers often do not follow the link when the click target is a button, so Download can save nothing. The button also does not set type="button". The copy and close buttons in this footer call preventDefault because a click submits the form; this control cannot do that without also cancelling the download. A click can therefore POST /api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable again after 2FA is already on, while the file may not download. Use a type="button" control that starts the blob download without wrapping a button in an anchor.

findings.title: Lost-access button also submits the disable form
findings.body: The new Lost access / Go back button is inside the disable Form and neither sets type="button" nor calls preventDefault. The real disable control in the same footer is type="submit", and the enable modal's non-submit actions call preventDefault because clicks in these forms submit. Clicking Lost access therefore also runs handleDisable. The click handler clears the code fields first, so the request is sent with an empty TOTP and backup code, the API returns a second-factor or incorrect-code error, and that error is shown just for switching modes. This disable path is untested. Set type="button" on the toggle.

findings.title: Backup-code auth is untested and the enable assertion cannot fail
findings.body: The enable-and-login test never closes the new backup-code step, so onEnable() does not run and the switch is not updated. It then asserts expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy(). isChecked() returns a Promise, and a Promise object is always truthy, so the assertion passes without 2FA being enabled. The test can also log out before the enable request finishes. The new steps only check that a download is named cal-backup-codes.txt and that a success toast appears; they do not read the file or use a code. Nothing covers login with a backup code, single-use consumption, a password-less backup-code attempt, or disabling 2FA with a backup code. Those are the paths with the auth and race bugs.

findings.title: Backup-code match is case-sensitive and only strips hyphens
findings.body: Stored codes are lowercase hex from randomBytes(5).toString("hex"), but login compares credentials.backupCode with indexOf after replaceAll("-", "") only. The disable handler in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61 does the same. Uppercase letters, spaces, or a different dash fail the match and are reported as an incorrect code. The field placeholder is XXXXX-XXXXX, and the recovery path is typing a saved code after losing the authenticator. Lowercase and strip non-hex characters before comparing in both handlers.

findings.title: Copy toast fires before the clipboard write succeeds
findings.body: The copy handler calls navigator.clipboard.writeText without awaiting or catching it, then immediately shows a success toast. writeText rejects when permission is denied or the clipboard API is missing. The user is told the codes were copied, closes the dialog, and cannot view them again. Await the write and toast only on success; show an error if it fails.

findings.title: Empty backup-code submit shows no error
findings.body: The login form sets noValidate, and the zod schema only validates email and password before passthrough, so the BackupCode required and minLength attributes are not enforced. Submitting Lost access with an empty code sends a falsy backupCode. The server treats that as not using a backup code, requires a TOTP code, and returns SecondFactorRequired. This handler only sets twoFactorRequired and does not set an error, so the submit looks like it did nothing. Validate backupCode on that step and show an error for an empty submission.

findings.title: Missing-backup-codes text points at a settings action that does not exist
findings.body: missing_backup_codes says to generate codes in settings. Users who enabled 2FA before this column existed, and anyone with null backupCodes, see this on login and when disabling 2FA. There is no settings action to generate codes while 2FA is already on: setup returns two-factor-already-enabled, and codes are only created during enable. The instruction cannot be followed. Tell them to disable and re-enable 2FA with the authenticator, or add a real regenerate action and then point at it.
